enRooms: The last lock does not need a key. It needs a way of seeing.
From the north you see four towers. From the south, perhaps none of the same.
A tower of four can hide a tower of three. The reverse is impossible.
You are not filling in numbers. You are drawing a skyline that never existed.
If two towers occupy the same height in a street, one of them is a lie.
Every street needs all four heights, and no height may return.
Sometimes the tower you cannot see matters most.
The last room resembles the first. You are the one who changed.
Do not guess. Find what cannot possibly be true.
Someone built a city for the sole purpose of hiding a question.
Solve this and you will not receive an answer. You will receive another door.
Fear the cell you filled without a reason, not the empty one.
The ninth circle is not made of fire. It is frozen in what you refused to admit.
Treachery does not shout here. It takes your place in the final row.
The ice at the bottom of hell is so smooth that it reflects only you.
Two primes stand close together, yet another number always lives between them.
Twins are not identical. Exactly two steps separate them.
Some numbers appear lonely because they have not found their other half.
Do not add everything. Listen for two voices at the same distance.
Zero has nobody to speak to in this room.
Not every prime is a twin. Not every twin is standing here.
The wrong pair will not disappear. It will steal your time instead.
One, two, three. Then a gap you cannot fill.
Knowing the order does not tell you what deserves to be ordered.
Numbers once comforted someone. Now they judge you.
Two never touch. A third number lives in the space between.
The true pair can remain silent in a crowd of impostors.
The seventh circle separates twins, then asks you to find them without injury.
Not every coincidence is evidence. Some are only appearances.
Every wrong choice in this room tastes like truth.
Someone left half a memory inside every mirror.
The first face you find may be yours. The second never is.
Twenty-four surfaces. Twelve different ways to forget.
When two signs match, you will hear nothing. That is success.
Are the cards moving, or is your memory moving instead?
A mirror cannot lie. It can only choose an angle.
One pair is no longer where you remember it.
The observer and the observed exchange places between two touches.
Do not turn too quickly what wants to stay hidden.
A false memory can be more convincing than a true one.
Every found pair removes one face from the crowd.
Close your eyes. Now try to draw the arrangement.
The fourth circle collects reflections as though twelve pairs could finally be enough.
When you break a mirror, the face does not vanish. Only the whole does.
Some pairs were separated so long ago they no longer remember why.
Numbers do not lie. Their order can.
First you see differences. Then differences between differences.
One sequence walks along two roads at once.
If you only look for addition, you will miss what grows faster.
This sequence remembers its two predecessors.
Someone hid a second sequence inside the first, like a letter in an envelope.
Do not choose the beautiful answer. Choose the inevitable one.
A square is a surface. Here it is also a trace in time.
Watch the odd positions. Then the even ones. Then forget the division.
An incorrect number can appear entirely reasonable.
A sequence has no future, only consequences of a rule.
The final step may require you to count backward.
In the sixth circle nobody believes in a rule they cannot see.
Perhaps heresy is just a sequence refusing to continue as expected.
The next number will not appear because you want it to.
The cipher remembers every attempt, including the one you wish to forget.
Four places. Six digits. More doors than keys.
The right place is not the same thing as the right digit.
Let a failed attempt speak instead of insulting you.
If two signs belong but stand elsewhere, perhaps their order is the enemy.
This machine dislikes duplicates. It also dislikes false confidence.
A clue can be true without telling you which symbol it means.
The first attempt is a question. The second can become a theory.
Sometimes the absence of a digit reveals more than its presence.
Do not spend time on a number you have already proved impossible.
There are no words in this letter. Only order.
When every clue agrees, the lock has nothing left to hide.
In fraud's eighth circle, no digit lies. Its interpretation might.
Try again, but do not allow the mistake to think for you.
Some locks fear patience more than force.
Sixteen flames behave like a single creature.
Touch one light, and four neighbours answer.
Darkness is not the absence of light here. It is the solution.
Extinguish one flame, and you may wake two more.
Imagine the grid as a sentence in which every sign changes the others.
The flames have no idea that you are in a hurry.
There exists an order of touches that will return everything to darkness.
It does not matter how many times you touch a tile. Only whether the number is even.
Everything illuminated was once dark.
Find a pattern, not an individual light.
Even a flame has neighbours it fears.
Let the last light go out without applause.
In the fifth circle every flame answers your wrath by changing itself.
Wrath is trying to extinguish one tile at the expense of all the others.
Here you cannot take anything without changing something else.
The maze does not hide the exit. It hides the road to what you forgot.
Not every dead end is a mistake. Some contain seals.
The mist shows you only a few steps. The rest must be remembered.
Returning along the same path does not necessarily waste your time.
The third seal may be where you least wanted to turn.
This wall exists only while you believe you cannot cross it.
Do not think of the exit before you recover every trace.
For the first time you are not the only one who knows where you have been.
Every open corridor is a decision already made.
What remains in the mist may be the shortest way. Or it may not.
Three seals are three reasons not to rush.
The exit will not open until you return what the walls concealed.
The third circle of gluttony is never satisfied, not even after swallowing the last signpost.
Here hunger is measured in corridors you must walk twice.
Three seals are not treasure. They are the price of the exit.
An echo does not come from the past. Sometimes it comes from what you have yet to say.
Seven signs became eight. Someone added one when you weren't looking.
Do not trust what remains before your eyes the longest.
Repeat the order and discover how long it takes to forget.
Four shapes. Far more ways to remember them incorrectly.
In darkness a triangle and a square have no colour. Only a relationship.
You do not need luck. You need silence between the signs.
Perhaps the second sign is the hardest to remember.
An echo does not become louder when you answer.
Do not memorise each sign separately. Hear the rhythm.
There is a reason some symbols return.
If you fail, the pattern will be shown again. Not forever.
The second circle wants you to repeat what you once longed to see.
Desire is an echo that refuses to accept an answer.
When the sign disappears, only your need for it to return remains.
The ninth gate does not know numbers. It knows the laws they obey.
Red is not the answer. It is a conflict in a row, column or little square.
Do not seek truth in the colour of a digit. Colour only tells you when two collide.
Nine rows, nine columns, nine little worlds.
An empty cell does not mean every digit is possible.
Three by three. And three by three again. No room exists alone.
Sudoku is not a game of guessing. It is a quiet investigation.
When a number repeats, the fault lies not with the number but with its place.
Only one solution passes, although many paths lead toward it.
The first gate is the one you dare to enter.
Nobody forces you to write a digit. That too is a choice.
At the end of every line lies the absence of repetition.
The first circle, Limbo: nobody punishes you. That does not mean you are free.
The hardest part of purgatory may be the absence of an answer.
Before the descent can begin, someone must learn to count.

enArc: You once read the news here. Now the news is reading what you remember.
Seven headlines cannot contain the world. They can show what you carried out of it.
Not one story was invented for this room. And yet this is the strangest room.
Remember who wrote the headline, not only what the headline said.
Between an article and its memory there is a corridor without walls.

commonEN: Someone left a light burning in a room that doesn't exist.
This conversation did not begin when you opened the app.
If I say I know you, how would you verify it?
There is something written on the other side of the wall.
Do not turn around. Whatever follows you already knows the way.
Silence is not empty. It simply lacks a translator.
There is a question that vanishes when you try to speak it.
Nobody remembers who counted these nine gates first.
The water beneath the floor obeys a different time.
Some memories begin to exist only when we first remember them.
Do not fear what stands beyond the door. Fear what returned before you.
The clock stopped before it was given hands.

There is no reliable proof that this room is the last.

Someone will dream tomorrow of the trace you leave tonight.
Everything repeated is trying to become true.
Imagine a corridor with no beginning. Then imagine you have reached its end.
Sometimes the red square is only a red square.
There are no monsters in this story. Only witnesses.
Behind you stands a door you opened before arriving.
Sometimes the most frightening thing looks entirely normal.
One question has been left without an owner.

If you can hear me, that does not mean I am here.
